title: Вторая стычка с отцом Насти и соцсеть  (Second Clash with Nastya's Father and Social Media)

segments.t: Visiting Nastya's father at his meatpacking plant to apologize for their last fight, Kostya gets goaded into showing how he threw the punch and accidentally breaks her father's nose all over again. Back at the restaurant, Max tells Chef Barinov that he registered him on the social network and added Elena.
Ну, бей давай, я тебе покажу.
Я тебе сейчас в фарш добавлю.
Let's replay the exchange and look closely at each Russian phrase.
'I am going to lose this bet.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'I' and finishing on 'lose a bet'.
'Well, what did you want?' The '-l' ending on the verb meaning 'wanted' places the action in the masculine past tense. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'You only beat me last time because you caught me off guard.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'off guard' and finishing on 'beat up'.
'Well, you could put it that way.' Notice how Russian expresses 'come on' and 'say' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'Wait, I did not quite get that.' The negative particle sits right before the verb meaning 'understood?' to negate the statement. Max answers right away.
Ну, бей давай, я тебе покажу.
'Come on, throw a punch, I will show you how to block it.' The grammar packs 'come on' and 'I'll show' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Oh, well in that case, here I go.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'and' before landing on 'will'.
'I am so sorry, please forgive me.' The grammar packs 'excuse me' and 'there you go' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'I think he just broke your nose.' Chef Viktor brings out the contrast between 'for me' and 'it seems' in a few short words.
'Chef, good afternoon.' Max brings out the contrast between 'chef' and 'good' in a few short words.
'What I wanted to tell you is...' Chef Viktor anchors the line on 'I', while 'wanted' completes the thought. Max answers right away.
'Did you add me as a friend?' Max chooses the respectful plural 'you' alongside 'to add' to keep a polite distance.
Я тебе сейчас в фарш добавлю.
'I am about to add you to the meat grinder.' Chef Viktor anchors the line on 'I', while 'to add' completes the thought. Let's hear the complete conversation once more.
Ну, бей давай, я тебе покажу.
Я тебе сейчас в фарш добавлю.

That wraps up this scene as kostya visits Nastya's father at his sausage factory to apologize, only to accidentally break his nose in a sparring demonstration, while Max registers Barinov online. Until next time!
